Existing repository ArcGIS adapter qualification: 9 of 13 aligned bounded cells complete (161 distinct IDs); four cells hold when duplicate idlote values make their returnIdsOnly object-ID manifests invalid. Raw full native geometry responses checked 176 rows and 15 repeated-ID groups; each repeated ID had one distinct full-polygon hash. Layer metadata exposed idlote as the sole OID, no GlobalID/uniqueIdInfo/alternate unique row ID. Offset mode also rejects the duplicate object IDs. 64 live requests returned HTTP 200; only idlote was requested. Exact-ID re-reads, forced one-ID pages, synthetic absence, nearby full footprint, complete binding and corrected bounded topology checks are recorded in macapa-runtime-qualification.json.
remainingUncertainty: The other nine bounded cells returned complete features (161 distinct idlote values); their exact-ID full-geometry re-reads, forced page-size-1 test, synthetic absence, nearby footprint read, proposal binding, and corrected topology checks passed. Four cells remain held solely on repeated OID manifests despite identical full polygon geometry for every repeated ID. The unchanged WUP-point query returned zero and a nearby lot is about 16 m from the point; that locator miss is informational, not a runtime gate. The official municipal SIT config directly names this layer, while its upstream hostname includes hml; host/production stability is also informational and unverified. Citywide completeness and title/ownership scope remain unknown.
nextStep: Keep runtime disabled until the municipal service exposes a unique feature-row OID/ID or corrects the view so each idlote is unique per returned feature; then re-run the existing adapter qualification. Root may independently review the positive nearby geometry finding. The WUP-point miss and hml hostname do not gate the source.
runtimeTechnicalHold: The existing adapter rejects four otherwise bounded full-geometry cell responses because returnIdsOnly repeats the layer’s sole OID field idlote. Raw geometry comparisons show one identical polygon hash per repeated ID; no alternate unique row ID or GlobalID appears in metadata. Offset paging also rejects the repeated ID. No adapter changes were made.
